0|6db541ae279bd4e76dbd939e5fbf298396166242|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"ibmvnic: Ensure login failure recovery is safe from other resets
If a login request fails
column2: the recovery process should be protected

column1: against parallel resets. It is a known issue that freeing and
registering CRQ's in quick succession can result in a failover CRQ from
the VIOS. Processing a failover during login recovery is dangerous for
two reasons:
1. This will result in two parallel initialization processes
cause serious issues during login.
2. It is possible that the failover CRQ is received but never executed.
We get notified of a pending failover through a transport event CRQ.
The reset is not performed until a INIT CRQ request is received.
Previously
column2: if CRQ init fails during login recovery

column1: irq is freed and the login process returned error. If failover_pending
is true (a transport event was received)
would never be able to process the reset since it cannot receive the
CRQ_INIT request due to the irq being freed. This leaved the device
in a inoperable state.
Therefore
column2: the login failure recovery process must be hardened against

column1: these possible issues. Possible failovers (due to quick CRQ free and
init) must be avoided and any issues during re-initialization should be
dealt with instead of being propagated up the stack. This logic is
similar to that of ibmvnic_probe().
Fixes: dff515a3e71d (""ibmvnic: Harden device login requests"")
